leads.source_status: Published 2023, online 2022; primary introduction and PDF checked.
leads.theorem: Miyanishi introduction theorem, small finite subgroups of GL2 of even order; explicit odd-map corollary on preprint page3.
leads.inward: With retained HCTANG2, all centered even four-variable unit-Hessian potentials have polynomial gradient inverses, in every degree. Proof in companion TeX.
leads.outward: Restricts possible HC4 failures to potentials without this centered parity symmetry; upgrades older bounded odd-plane cotangent tests.
leads.missing: Full HC4 remains open. The universal cotangent reduction is the retained unreviewed Tang input; explicitly cotangent odd-base cases need only the published plane theorem. No new priority claim.
leads.adoption: No 2110.06709 or equivariant-Jacobian citation found in scanned active/archive Markdown; archive HC4_SOURCE_DUAL_BIGRADING.md uses odd plane pairs only with a degree-bound/Moh argument.
leads.next_step: Have the HC4 owner audit and integrate the exact parity corollary and retain the central involution/small-group hypotheses. Avoid treating arbitrary even-order deck groups as source equivariance.

leads.theorem: Classical Manin kernel discussion and Proposition2.15; contrast Proposition2.14 for the different map mu_A.
leads.inward: Compute the actual boundary section obstruction using its classical Manin class on the abelian part and logarithmic derivatives on a split torus. The split product case has a precise criterion proved in the companion TeX.
leads.outward: Connects an all-order moment obstruction to differential algebraic groups and inhomogeneous Picard-Fuchs classes; gives a concrete normal-function obstruction beyond a scalar norm.
leads.missing: Show eventual exceptional purity forces vanishing of that actual class. Constant trace must be separated correctly. Nonsplit semiabelian extensions require their extension data; higher toric rank is not automatically covered by the semiabelian Ax-Lindemann results in this paper.
leads.adoption: No identifier citation found in scanned Markdown.
leads.next_step: Express the actual rank-one boundary 1-motive section in the universal vectorial extension and identify its CLASSICAL differential class; keep all recomposition branches.

leads.theorem: Theorems2.2.1/2.2.3 and5.1.1; standing assumptions include no fixed part on any finite cover and Zariski density of the section-generated subgroup.
leads.inward: A differential rank test on the actual abelian section could detect whether it moves; rank is controlled by a contracted Kodaira-Spencer map.
leads.outward: Relates the exceptional moment problem to Betti leaves, functional transcendence and monodromy of algebraic sections.
leads.missing: The full boundary family includes toric and constant parts. Do not apply a no-fixed-part theorem to the full semiabelian object. Base dimension one prevents full rank2g for g>1; zero rank is the relevant possible target.
leads.adoption: No identifier or Betti-map citation found in scanned Markdown.
leads.next_step: First isolate the relevant abelian trace/quotient and generated subgroup; test whether purity has any consequence for the actual Betti derivative rather than counting torsion specializations.

leads.source_status: Primary Hain Section13 and Brosnan-Pearlstein introduction inspected.
leads.theorem: Hain Theorem13.1 supplies a nonnegative (1,1) form for a polarized weight-minus-one normal function; Corollary13.3 uses complete curves.
leads.inward: Seek an energy/curvature identity for the actual abelian boundary normal function; positivity might convert purity into a vanishing infinitesimal invariant.
leads.outward: Bridges complex moment identities with height pairings, biextension metrics and boundary intersection data.
leads.missing: No such purity-to-energy identity is proved. Our base is punctured affine line, so one cannot apply the complete-curve integral conclusion without controlling boundary contributions and height jumps. Torus extensions require separate treatment.
leads.adoption: No identifiers found in scanned Markdown.
leads.next_step: Derive the correct polarized form and boundary terms from the actual Picard complex before any positivity argument.

leads.source_status: Published 2016; primary preprint PDF and Section7.2 checked.
leads.theorem: Relative Manin-Mumford for semiabelian surfaces identifies Ribet sections as exceptional configurations.
leads.inward: Protect the constant-point argument against replacing it by torsion density or a scalar norm; semi-constant extensions have real exceptional behavior.
leads.outward: The retained Long composite gives a concrete norm-one torus/Pell-type period countercontrol, proved algebraically in the companion TeX.
leads.missing: The relative Manin-Mumford theorem is about torsion specializations, not a blanket constant-type test. Ribet sections do not refute the retained constant-point criterion. Our elementary toric example is not itself a Ribet section.
leads.adoption: No identifier or Ribet citation found in scanned Markdown.
leads.next_step: Keep abelian trace, toric characters and the extension class visible; test every proposed simplification against the existing all-branch norm-one example.

leads.source_status: Published; primary publisher abstract verified. Author PDF text extraction is garbled; precise general saturation version not adopted here.
leads.theorem: For a prime in a commutative Noetherian ring, equivalence of adic and symbolic topologies implies linear equivalence. No finite symbolic-Rees hypothesis in that statement.
leads.inward: A possible replacement for the disproved universal scalar-time equation: realize the actual apolar deficit topology as the relevant ideal-topology comparison, then use a qualitative-to-linear theorem.
leads.outward: Would convert the formal-operator question into a commutative-algebra regularity problem rather than holonomicity.
leads.missing: The ACTUAL power annihilators are not known to be symbolic powers/saturations of powers of one ideal. Arbitrary nested filtrations do not qualify; ordinary nesting is insufficient.
leads.adoption: No Swanson citation found in scanned Markdown.
leads.next_step: Construct or rule out this exact representation using the suspended embedded apolar ideals. Do not assume a finite Rees algebra or import the theorem directly into an arbitrary filtration.

leads.theorem: Uniform linear Chevalley bounds for analytic maps regular in the sense of Gabrielov; refinements along proper fibres and formally Nash sets.
leads.inward: An actual realization of apolar-height comparison as an order-of-pullback estimate would provide a unit-stable route to linear bounds.
leads.outward: Connects the operator gap to analytic regularity and formal relation ideals.
leads.missing: No such map has been constructed. Arbitrary formal symbols need not converge; Gabrielov regularity is an extra requirement, not a consequence of nesting.
leads.adoption: No identifier or Izumi citation found; unrelated uses of Chevalley appear elsewhere.
leads.next_step: Identify a concrete analytic/formally Nash map for a legitimate source class, or use counterexamples to show this route cannot cover the unrestricted symbols.

leads.missing: The finite normalization trace dual is not automatically the logarithmic-residue module of its branch curve. Establish the exact restriction/duality map and retain Tor/conductor gluing, rather than equating them from generic valuations.
